title: Kepler's Postscript on Bartolus, September 1622
author: Johannes Kepler
source: The postscript to Johannes Kepler's letter to Philipp Müller written at Linz after 3 September 1622, in which Kepler questions the astrologer Abraham Bartolus about his use of harmonic intervals as astrological aspects. The letter itself survives at Pulkovo and was printed by Hanschius (*Epistolae*, 1718); the separate postscript is in the Bibliothèque nationale, Paris (Nouv. acq. lat. 1635, fol. 104), with a copy at fols. 105–108. First printed in *Nova Kepleriana* 4, ed. Walther von Dyck and Max Caspar, Abhandlungen der Bayerischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, Math.-naturw. Abteilung 31, no. 1 (Munich, 1927), 30–33.
transcribed_from: the page images of the 1927 printing.
summary: Kepler asks the astrologer Abraham Bartolus, through Müller, on what grounds he takes harmonic intervals as effective aspects, and sets out his own method: aspects arise from the division of the circle by inscribed figures, and the harmonies of the monochord only derive from them.

notes.note: Aspects of 30° and 150°, two of the new aspects Kepler added to Ptolemy's five.
Literally “behind the *principes*”, the second line of a Roman battle order.
